- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.3), model tends to undercorrect; increase forecast slightly to avoid excessive downward bias.  
- After sharp price spikes, model often overshoots downward; apply a mild upward bias to counteract lagged mean reversion.  
- In periods of high volatility or sentiment swings, model overreacts to recent moves; dampen forecast sensitivity to recent history.  
- If sentiment is positive but price is trending down, model may ignore sentiment; adjust forecast upward to reflect sentiment-driven support.  
- For 30-day horizons, model frequently underestimates mean reversion; add a small upward bias toward historical mean if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative over 3–5 days, model tends to forecast lower than true outcome; apply a small upward correction to avoid overcorrection.
